nodes.summary: For every set $K$ of finite ordered graphs, the decision problem of the encodings of $K$ (the bitstrings that decode to a member $(n, T)$ of $K$ whose edge table $T$ has length exactly $n^2$) belongs to $\mathrm{NL}$ if and only if $K$ is definable in first-order logic with transitive closure.
nodes.title: Immerman: FO + transitive closure is NL on ordered structures

nodes.summary: In an ordered graph with domain $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$, relation symbol $0$ holds of a list of elements exactly when the list is $[a, b]$ with $a < b$, relation symbol $1$ holds exactly when the list is $[a, b]$ and there is an edge from $a$ to $b$, and every other relation symbol holds of no list.
nodes.title: Order and edge relations as FO + TC relation symbols

nodes.summary: A set $K$ of ordered graphs is FO + TC-definable when there are an FO + TC formula $\varphi$ and a boolean $b$ such that for every ordered graph $(n, T)$ whose edge table $T$ has length exactly $n^2$: if $n > 0$, then $(n, T) \in K$ exactly when $(n, T)$ satisfies $\varphi$, and if $n = 0$, then $(n, T) \in K$ exactly when $b$ is true.
nodes.title: Definability in FO + TC

nodes.summary: For an ordered graph $(n, T)$ with edge table $T$ and elements $a, b < n$, there is an edge from $a$ to $b$ when the entry of $T$ at position $a n + b$ is true; positions beyond the end of $T$ count as false.
nodes.title: Edge relation of an ordered graph for FO + TC

nodes.summary: For a set $K$ of ordered graphs, this is the decision problem that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of pairs of a natural number and a list of booleans, to some ordered graph $(n, T) \in K$ whose edge table $T$ has length exactly $n^2$.
nodes.title: Encodings of a class of ordered graphs

nodes.summary: Fix an ordered graph with domain $D = \{0, \dots, n - 1\}$, an assignment $\rho$ of an element of $D$ to each variable index and an assignment $S$ of a relation on lists of elements of $D$ to each relation symbol. The truth value of a formula is defined by recursion. The equation between variables $i$ and $j$ holds when $\rho(i) = \rho(j)$. Relation symbol $i$ applied to variables $j_1, \dots, j_k$ holds when $S_i$…
nodes.title: Evaluation of FO + TC formulas

nodes.summary: The FO + TC formula $\mathrm{TC}(\varphi; (0, 1), (2, 3))$ of arity $2$ whose body $\varphi$ states that relation symbol $1$ (the edge relation) holds of variables $0, 2$ and of variables $1, 3$. In the body, variables $0, 1$ are the source pair and $2, 3$ the target pair, so a step moves both components along an edge at the same time, and the formula expresses that the pair of outer variables $(2, 3)$ is reachable…
nodes.title: Example: simultaneous reachability of pairs in FO + TC

nodes.summary: The FO + TC formula $\mathrm{TC}(\varphi; (1), (2))$ of arity $1$ whose body $\varphi$ is $E(0, 1) \lor (E(0, 2) \land E(2, 1))$, where $E$ is relation symbol $1$ (the edge relation). In the body, variable $0$ is the source, variable $1$ the target, and variable $2$ is outer variable $0$, shifted by $2$; the endpoint arguments $1$ and $2$ are outer variables, not shifted. So the formula expresses that outer…
nodes.title: Example: parameterized transitive closure in FO + TC

nodes.summary: An ordered graph with nonempty domain $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ satisfies an FO + TC formula $\varphi$ when $\varphi$ evaluates to true with every variable assigned the element $0$, relation symbol $0$ interpreted as the order $<$ and relation symbol $1$ as the edge relation (both only on two-element lists), and every other relation symbol interpreted as the empty relation.
nodes.title: Satisfaction of an FO + TC formula in an ordered graph

nodes.summary: FO + TC formulas, with variables and relation symbols indexed by natural numbers, are built from equations between two variables and relation symbols applied to lists of variables by negation, conjunction, disjunction, existential quantification (which binds variable $0$, de Bruijn style) and transitive closure $\mathrm{TC}(\varphi; \bar u, \bar v)$ of a formula $\varphi$ applied to two lists $\bar u$, $\bar v$ of…
nodes.title: Formulas of first-order logic with transitive closure

nodes.summary: An ordered graph is encoded as a pair $(n, e)$ of a natural number $n$, the domain size, and a finite list $e$ of booleans of arbitrary length, the edge table in row-major order. It is read as the graph on $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$, ordered numerically, with an edge from $a$ to $b$ when the entry of $e$ at position $an + b$ is true; a missing entry counts as false.
nodes.title: Ordered graphs for first-order logic with transitive closure

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
